input: Reshingle the garden shed roof this spring

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The current roof condition determines whether only shingles need replacing or if decking, underlayment, or structural repairs are also required, which significantly changes the workload and cost.
Whether this is a solo DIY job, a family/friend group effort, or involves hiring a contractor changes the plan entirely — skill requirements, tools needed, and scheduling all shift.
The size and pitch of the shed roof dictates how much material to buy, how long the job will take, and what safety measures (ladders, harness) are needed.
A firm budget ceiling determines what shingle grade and type are realistic, and whether professional help is even on the table.
Whether tools (nail gun, roofing nailer, pry bar) and materials are already on hand or need to be sourced is the gating factor for when work can actually begin.
Shingle type (asphalt 3-tab, architectural, wood, metal panels) affects cost, longevity, appearance, and installation method — a core material decision.
Knowing what 'done well' means — waterproofing only, a certain aesthetic, a target completion date — sets the quality bar and informs which steps are non-negotiable.

gold.taskTitle: Reshingle the garden shed roof this spring
gold.taskDescription: Remove the existing roofing and install new shingles on a garden shed roof before the end of spring.

questions.title: What is the current condition of the existing roof?
questions.description: Find out if the issue is just worn shingles or if there is underlying damage to the decking or structure that needs addressing first.

questions.title: Will you do this yourself or hire someone?
questions.description: Determine whether this is a DIY project or a contractor job, as this changes every downstream step in the plan.

questions.title: How big is the shed roof and what is its pitch?
questions.description: Capture the approximate dimensions and slope of the roof to estimate materials, time, and safety requirements.

questions.title: What is your total budget for this project?
questions.description: Establish a spending ceiling so material grade, shingle type, and labour options can be scoped appropriately.

questions.title: Do you already have the tools and materials on hand?
questions.description: Identify whether a procurement step is needed before work can begin, and flag any tool rentals or purchases required.

questions.title: What type of shingles are you planning to use?
questions.description: Nail down the chosen shingle material (asphalt 3-tab, architectural, wood shake, metal panels, etc.) as this drives installation method and cost.

questions.title: What does a successful finished roof look like to you?
questions.description: Clarify the quality bar — purely functional and watertight, visually matching the house, completed by a specific spring date, or something else.
